title: Phylogeography and historical biogeography of the widespread garden treeboa Corallus hortulana (Squamata, Boidae)
content:
Abstract
Biogeographic studies of widely distributed species allow us to understand possible dispersal routes and the influence of changes in climate and landscape in shaping the current ranges of occurrence of different populations. The objective of our work was to understand the limits and structure of lineages and the possible area of origin in addition to the biogeographic events important for the dispersal and diversification of the arboreal snake Corallus hortulana. We found six well-defined and structured lineages of C. hortulana distributed throughout South American ecosystems with older divergence estimates compared to other studies. Furthermore, the emergence of C. hortulana east of the Amazon and its westward dispersal are distinct compared to most studied taxa that diversified in this region. We propose the hypothesis that an Amazonian arboreal snake may have favoured and potentially utilized large rivers and the ocean to promote dispersal throughout South America, possibly using natural rafts to cross rivers and occupy islands in the Caribbean Atlantic Ocean.
